subject: Charge reconciliation: duplicate batched requests detected (OV-4321)
messages:
From: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@ovaltine.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@ovaltine.io
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Strange spike in mid-cycle charges — can you help?

Hi Markus,

We just received the provisional mid-cycle bill and see a large charge labeled as 'batched generation — 06/01'. It looks like ~1.2M tokens were charged in a 10-minute window between 03:12–03:22 UTC. That doesn't correlate with anything our traffic logs show — our ingestion team only sees a couple of short batches during that window.

Can Redwood share the breakdown (per-request IDs, model, route) so we can reconcile on our side? We're evaluating whether to pause a portion of our pipeline until this is clarified.

I've attached a CSV from our side (ovaltine_ingest_snapshot.csv) and cc'd billing for visibility.

Thanks,
Jessica Lopez
Billing Operations | OvalTine Health
--
Attachment: ovaltine_ingest_snapshot.csv (csv, 42KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@ovaltine.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Strange spike in mid-cycle charges — can you help?

Hi Jessica — thanks for flagging this and for the CSV. We pulled the preliminary logs and there are two suspiciously similar client_request_ids that show up repeatedly in your account during that 03:12–03:22 UTC window: c-89f4a7 and c-89f4a7-dup (the latter is an internal dedupe tag from our front door).

Quick context: your integration is hitting our batch/generate route with an aggressive retry/backoff pattern for timeouts. Under certain conditions (backend slowdown + client retry), our gateway has historically created duplicate batch jobs with separate token accounting before the KV cache was reattached. We've implemented mitigations but we need to investigate whether this incident is one of those edge cases.

I'll run a full token-level export and share a zipped log with request-level metadata. In parallel, can you confirm whether you were running a bulk import job around that time or had any of your workers restart?

Markus
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: redwood_token_logs_ov-4321_20270601.zip (zip, 3.1MB)
From: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@ovaltine.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@ovaltine.io
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Strange spike in mid-cycle charges — can you help?

Thanks Markus — our ops lead confirms there was a short bulk import that started at 03:05 UTC (file: user_profiles_batch_0601.ndjson) that ran for ~7 min. No planned restarts. She also says some workers did log a handful of transient HTTP 504s right at 03:12 UTC and retried once.

I'm attaching the import manifest and a short snippet of our client logs showing the retry pattern. If you can map those client request ids to your export it would be helpful.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Jessica
--
Attachment: user_profiles_batch_0601.manifest (txt, 2KB)
Attachment: ov_client_retry_snippet.txt (txt, 4KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@ovaltine.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange spike in mid-cycle charges — can you help?

Hi Jessica — Connor from Redwood Support here. We correlated your client-side timestamps with our internal trace and found that 03:12:14–03:12:46 UTC contains a cluster of 12 batch requests where the gateway generated two separate execution records for the same logical batch id (internal tag: dedupe-miss). Each execution consumed token counts independently before a late dedupe reconciliation marked one as redundant. Unfortunately our billing pipeline is downstream of dedupe reconciliation in some fast-path flows — so the initial token writes were included in the provisional bill.

What this means practically: we have evidence of duplicate charge writes for the dedupe-miss executions. Our proposed remediation steps: 1) issue a mid-cycle credit for the redundant tokens, 2) provide a per-request CSV mapping (we attached a trimmed export), and 3) update your account to a protection flag that delays billing writes for 90s while dedupe reconciles for high-volume batch customers.

Would you like us to proceed with the credits immediately or do you prefer a joint review with your finance team first?

Connor
Customer Support Engineer | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: redwood_trimmed_export_ov-4321.csv (csv, 120KB)
From: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@ovaltine.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@ovaltine.io
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Strange spike in mid-cycle charges — can you help?

Thanks Connor — that aligns with what our engineers saw (retries + a few 504s). We'd like Redwood to proceed with the mid-cycle credit for redundant tokens and the protective billing write delay. Please run the credit for the redundant usage and send a one-line confirmation once it's posted so our AR team can reconcile.

Also, two quick follow-ups for accounting: 1) will that credit be itemized on the June invoice or as a separate line item? 2) do we need to amend any VAT reporting given the retroactive credit? OvalTine is in the US but has EU subsidiaries — want to make sure the VAT treatment stays clean.

Best,
Jessica
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@ovaltine.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange spike in mid-cycle charges — can you help?

Hi Jessica — quick update from our finance ops and tax team:

1) Credit posting: We will post the mid-cycle credit as a separate line item labelled 'Duplicate execution credit (OV-4321)' and apply it against your June statement. Expect the post within 48 hours and we will send a credit confirmation email with the accounting reference number.

2) VAT treatment: Because the credit is an adjustment to billed usage and not a separate taxable supply, our standard practice is to issue the credit with the same tax metadata as the original charge and include an explanatory note for your EU subsidiaries. If OvalTine needs a VAT-only correction document for local reporting, we can generate that on request — please let us know the EU entity/entities affected and the invoice numbers to amend.

3) Longer-term mitigation: Markus and Connor will turn on the 90s billing-write delay for your account under a temporary protection policy while we finalize a code fix that eliminates the dedupe-miss. We'll schedule a short call to review telemetry and the protection window.

I'll follow up with the accounting reference once the credit posts.

Thanks — and sorry for the disruption,
Grace O'Connor
Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
